drhp.business: Panacea Biotec manufactures recombinant, bacterial and viral vaccine drug substances at Lalru (Punjab) and fills them into finished vaccines at Baddi (Himachal Pradesh), selling WHO-prequalified combination and oral polio vaccines to multilateral agencies, national governments and India's private market. Through PBPL it also makes oral-solid, semi-solid, liquid and cytotoxic injectable pharmaceutical formulations for ~40 export markets, and sells paediatric nutrition and baby-care brands in India through chemists, distributors, e-commerce and its own D2C portal.

drhp.one_liner: Indian paediatric vaccine maker supplying combination and oral polio vaccines to UNICEF, PAHO and the Government of India, with pharmaceutical formulations and nutrition/baby-care businesses run through its wholly owned subsidiary Panacea Biotec Pharma Limited (PBPL).

plants.capacity: wP and DT capacity being scaled up to 70 million doses per annum (facility expansion completed; DT regulatory approval pending)
plants.role: Vaccine drug substance (bacterial, viral and recombinant blocks: r-HBsAg, tetanus toxoid, Hib-TT conjugate, whole-cell pertussis, diphtheria toxoid, dengue viral drug substance); operating since 2002

plants.capacity: Two independent formulation suites and three filling lines; production block approx. 2,800 m² per floor; warehouse/cold storage block approx. 4,702 m²
plants.role: Vaccine drug product (formulation and filling; PFS, single- and multi-dose vials, lyophilized vaccines); operating since 2008
Pharmaceutical formulations (oral solids, semi-solids, liquids); operational since 2006
Cytotoxic / oncology injectables (liquid and lyophilized filling lines)
Nutrition products (ChilRun range); operational since April 2023

Nutrition & baby care (PBPL): NikoMom® Baby Skin Care (massage oil, head-to-toe wash, daily lotion, diaper rash cream)
Pharmaceutical formulations (PBPL): Oral solids (conventional, controlled/delayed release, bilayer, chewable, fast-dissolving tablets and capsules)
Cytotoxic / oncology injectables incl. nano-particle and liposomal lyophilized products
Vaccine pipeline: DengiAll® (single-dose tetravalent dengue vaccine, Phase III)
NuCoVac®-11 (11-valent pneumococcal conjugate, Phase III completed)
VaxiPox (multi-epitope recombinant mpox candidate, with BRIC-THSTI)
Recombinant nanoparticle broadly protective Beta-coronavirus candidate (with BRIC-THSTI)

risks.note: The Company describes itself as one of the largest vaccine suppliers to UNICEF and PAHO and has supplied institutional customers and national governments for over two decades, with new supply awards such as a CMSS Td vaccine award; procurement decisions by a small set of institutional buyers therefore drive its vaccine volumes.
risks.risk: Dependence on multilateral and government buyers

risks.note: DengiAll® launch is expected by 2027-28 only after completing the Phase III trial (two-year participant follow-up) and receiving regulatory approvals; wider supply of pipeline and licensed products to UN agencies depends on obtaining WHO prequalification.

Trade receivables sit in medium- and high-credit-risk categories; the Company mitigates via bank guarantees/letters of credit for high-risk customers and treats receivables as in default only when two years past due.

MD&A states the global pharmaceutical growth outlook is subject to pricing and reimbursement pressures, changes in healthcare and trade policies, and geopolitical uncertainty — relevant to PBPL's export-led formulations business.
risks.risk: Pharma pricing, policy and trade headwinds

- Hungary's NCPHP found PBPL's Baddi facility non-compliant with GMP after a January 2026 inspection, revoking all its GMP certificates and proposing a halt on non-vital product supplies; restoration depends on a re-inspection that PBPL has requested after implementing CAPA.
- The financial-risk note classes loans (including loans to related parties) in the high-credit-risk category and measures loss allowance on them as lifetime expected credit losses, based on the counterparties' creditworthiness.
- The Company describes itself as one of the largest vaccine suppliers to UNICEF and PAHO and has supplied institutional customers and national governments for over two decades, with new supply awards such as a CMSS Td vaccine award; procurement decisions by a small set of institutional buyers therefore drive its vaccine volumes.
- DengiAll® launch is expected by 2027-28 only after completing the Phase III trial (two-year participant follow-up) and receiving regulatory approvals; wider supply of pipeline and licensed products to UN agencies depends on obtaining WHO prequalification.
- Trade receivables sit in medium- and high-credit-risk categories; the Company mitigates via bank guarantees/letters of credit for high-risk customers and treats receivables as in default only when two years past due.
- MD&A states the global pharmaceutical growth outlook is subject to pricing and reimbursement pressures, changes in healthcare and trade policies, and geopolitical uncertainty — relevant to PBPL's export-led formulations business.
